name: JEE Advanced
conductingBody: Joint Admission Board (JAB) – one of seven zonal IITs by rotation
approxCandidates: Top ≈2.5 lakh JEE Main qualifiers eligible; ≈1.8–1.9 lakh register and appear
eligibility: Among top ≈2.5 lakh in JEE Main (category-wise); max 2 attempts in consecutive years; born on/after 1 Oct 2002 (5-yr relaxation SC/ST/PwD); Class 12 in 2026 or 2027

notification.summary: The 2026 exam was held by IIT Roorkee on 17 May 2026. As of 10 Oct 2026 the JAB had not announced the organising IIT or dates for JEE Advanced 2027 (IIT Delhi is widely expected by rotation but unconfirmed); the exam is expected in the second or third week of May 2027.

importantDates.date: Late Apr – early May 2027 (expected, after JEE Main Session 2 result)

pattern.notes: Two compulsory 3-hour papers on the same day; the structure changes every year. A recent Paper 1 (2025) had per subject: 4 single-correct MCQs (+3/−1), 3 one-or-more-correct MCQs (+4 with partial marking/−2), 6 non-negative integer questions (+4/0) and 4 matching-list MCQs (+3/−1); some 2026 analyses report 17 questions per subject. This mock simulates the single-correct MCQ format (+3/−1) only.

trendAnalysis.summary: JEE Advanced remains concept-integrating and lengthy; Mathematics and Physics have alternated as the toughest subject (Physics reported toughest in 2026, Mathematics in 2024). Calculus, probability, matrices and vectors/3D dominate Mathematics; mechanics (rotation, fluids), electrostatics/magnetism and modern physics dominate Physics. Chemistry is the most scoring section but physical chemistry numericals and mechanism-based organic questions have grown, while inorganic stays NCERT-anchored (coordination, p-block). Integer-type and matching questions keep guessing low; cut-offs have been around 25–30% of total marks for the common rank list.

resources.notes: Every organising IIT publishes both question papers (English and Hindi) and the provisional/final answer keys on jeeadv.ac.in; older years are in the site's archive section. An official mock CBT link is posted on jeeadv.ac.in before registration.

questions.question: A screw gauge has pitch 0.5 mm and 50 circular divisions. With the jaws closed it reads +0.03 mm. When a wire is held between the jaws, the main scale shows 3.0 mm and the circular scale division 26 coincides with the reference line. The corrected diameter of the wire is
questions.explanation: Least count = 0.5/50 = 0.01 mm. Observed = 3.0 + 26 × 0.01 = 3.26 mm. Positive zero error is subtracted: 3.26 − 0.03 = 3.23 mm.

questions.question: In a simple-pendulum experiment g = 4π²L/T². If L is measured with 1% error and T with 2% error, the maximum percentage error in g is
A projectile is launched from level ground at 20 m/s at 60° above the horizontal. After what time is its velocity perpendicular to its initial velocity? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: v·u = u² − gt·u sinθ = 0 ⇒ t = u/(g sinθ) = 20/(10 × √3/2) = 4/√3 ≈ 2.31 s, which is less than the flight time 2√3 s, so it occurs in flight.

questions.question: Block A (2 kg) rests on block B (4 kg), which lies on a frictionless floor. The coefficient of friction between A and B is 0.5. A horizontal force F is applied to B. The largest F for which the blocks move together is (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Friction can give A at most a = μg = 5 m/s². Moving together: F = (2 + 4) × 5 = 30 N.

questions.question: A ball of mass m moving with speed v collides head-on and elastically with a stationary ball of mass 2m. The fraction of the initial kinetic energy transferred to the heavier ball is
questions.explanation: Fraction transferred = 4m₁m₂/(m₁ + m₂)² = 4·m·2m/(3m)² = 8/9.

questions.question: A uniform disc of radius R spinning about its axis with angular speed ω₀ (centre at rest) is gently placed upright on its rim on a rough horizontal floor. When it starts pure rolling, the speed of its centre is
questions.explanation: Friction acts at the contact point, so angular momentum about that point is conserved: ½MR²ω₀ = ½MR²ω + MvR with v = ωR ⇒ ½ω₀ = (3/2)ω ⇒ ω = ω₀/3, v = ω₀R/3.

questions.question: A solid cylinder and a thin hollow cylinder of equal mass and radius roll without slipping from rest down the same incline from the same height. The ratio of their times of descent (t_solid : t_hollow) is
questions.explanation: a = g sinθ/(1 + k²/R²): solid 2g sinθ/3, hollow g sinθ/2. t ∝ 1/√a ⇒ t_s/t_h = √((1/2)/(2/3)) = √(3/4) = √3/2.

questions.question: A satellite moves in a circular orbit with speed v. The minimum additional speed it must be given (along its velocity) to escape the Earth's gravity is
questions.explanation: Escape speed at the orbit radius is √2 times the orbital speed, so the extra speed needed is √2v − v = (√2 − 1)v.

questions.question: Water rises to a height h in a capillary tube on the ground. If the same experiment is done in a lift accelerating upward at g/2, the height of rise becomes
questions.explanation: h = 2T cosθ/(rρg_eff). In the lift g_eff = g + g/2 = 3g/2, so h' = h/(3/2) = 2h/3.

questions.question: An ideal monatomic gas undergoes a process in which pressure is directly proportional to volume (P ∝ V). Its molar heat capacity for this process is
questions.explanation: P ∝ V means PV⁻¹ = constant, a polytropic process with n = −1. C = C_v − R/(n − 1) = 3R/2 + R/2 = 2R.

questions.question: Two rods of the same length and cross-section, with thermal conductivities K and 2K, are joined end to end. The effective thermal conductivity of the composite rod is
questions.explanation: Series thermal resistances: 2L/(K_eff A) = L/(KA) + L/(2KA) ⇒ K_eff = 2·K·2K/(K + 2K) = 4K/3.

questions.question: The fundamental frequency of a pipe closed at one end is 100 Hz. The second harmonic of an open pipe of the same length is
questions.explanation: Closed pipe: v/4L = 100 Hz ⇒ v/2L = 200 Hz is the open pipe's fundamental. Its second harmonic is 400 Hz.

questions.question: A parallel-plate capacitor of capacitance C₀ (air) has a dielectric slab of constant 4 inserted, filling the full plate area and half the gap thickness. The new capacitance is
A solid non-conducting sphere of radius R carries charge Q uniformly through its volume. The ratio of the electric field at distance R/2 from the centre to that at distance 2R is
questions.explanation: Inside: E = kQr/R³ = kQ/(2R²) at R/2. Outside: E = kQ/(4R²) at 2R. Ratio = 2 : 1.

questions.question: A capacitor is charged through a resistor from an ideal battery; the time constant is τ. The energy stored in the capacitor reaches half of its final value at time
A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field with its velocity at 60° to the field. The ratio of the pitch of its helical path to the radius of the helix is
questions.explanation: Pitch = 2πm v cosθ/(qB); radius = m v sinθ/(qB). Ratio = 2π cot 60° = 2π/√3.

questions.question: In an L–R circuit connected to a battery at t = 0, the magnetic energy stored in the inductor reaches one-quarter of its final value at time (τ = L/R)
questions.explanation: U ∝ i², so U = U_f/4 when i = i₀/2: 1 − e^(−t/τ) = 1/2 ⇒ t = τ ln 2.

questions.question: A thin plano-convex lens (refractive index 1.5) has its curved surface of radius 20 cm. Its plane surface is silvered. The system behaves like a concave mirror of focal length
questions.explanation: Lens focal length f = R/(μ − 1) = 40 cm. Silvered plane face (P_m = 0): P = 2/f = 1/20 cm⁻¹, so F = 20 cm, equivalent to R/(2(μ − 1)).

questions.question: The activity of a radioactive sample falls to 1/16 of its initial value in 40 days. The mean life of the nuclide is approximately
questions.explanation: 1/16 = (1/2)⁴ ⇒ 4 half-lives = 40 days ⇒ T½ = 10 days. Mean life τ = T½/0.693 ≈ 14.4 days.

questions.question: When light of wavelength 400 nm falls on a metal, the stopping potential is V₀. If 300 nm light is used instead, the stopping potential increases by approximately (hc = 1240 eV nm)
questions.explanation: ΔV = (hc/e)(1/300 − 1/400) = 1240 × (1/1200) ≈ 1.03 V; the work function cancels.

questions.question: What volume of 0.1 M KMnO₄ is needed to oxidise 50 mL of 0.5 M FeSO₄ in acidic medium?
questions.explanation: MnO₄⁻ + 5Fe²⁺ + 8H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 5Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O. Fe²⁺ = 25 mmol needs 5 mmol MnO₄⁻ = 50 mL of 0.1 M.

questions.question: According to Bohr's model, the energy of the electron in the third orbit of Li²⁺ is
Which of the following has the largest number of lone pairs on the central atom?
questions.explanation: Lone pairs on central atom: XeF₂ = 3, ClF₃ = 2, IF₅ = 1, SF₄ = 1.

questions.question: Which pair of species is isostructural?
questions.explanation: XeF₄ and ICl₄⁻ both have 4 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs and are square planar. SF₄ is see-saw, NH₃ pyramidal vs BF₃ planar, SO₃²⁻ pyramidal vs SO₃ planar.

questions.question: Two moles of an ideal gas expand isothermally and reversibly at 300 K from 10 L to 100 L. The work done on the gas is (R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
The pH of a 0.1 M aqueous solution of sodium acetate is (pKa of acetic acid = 4.74, 25 °C)
questions.explanation: Salt of weak acid and strong base: pH = 7 + ½(pKa + log C) = 7 + ½(4.74 − 1) = 8.87.

questions.question: N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g) is 20% dissociated at equilibrium at a total pressure of 1 atm. Kp for the reaction is approximately
questions.explanation: Mole fractions: NO₂ = 2α/(1 + α), N₂O₄ = (1 − α)/(1 + α). Kp = 4α²P/(1 − α²) = 4(0.04)(1)/0.96 ≈ 0.167 atm.

questions.question: Given Λ°m (S cm² mol⁻¹): HCl = 426, NaCl = 126, CH₃COONa = 91. Λ°m of CH₃COOH is
questions.explanation: By Kohlrausch's law: Λ°(CH₃COOH) = Λ°(CH₃COONa) + Λ°(HCl) − Λ°(NaCl) = 91 + 426 − 126 = 391.

questions.question: The rate constant of a reaction doubles when the temperature rises from 300 K to 310 K. The activation energy is approximately (R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
An ideal solution contains 1 mol of A (P°A = 100 torr) and 3 mol of B (P°B = 60 torr). The mole fraction of A in the vapour in equilibrium is
Which oxoacid of phosphorus contains two P–H bonds?
questions.explanation: Hypophosphorous acid H₃PO₂ has one P–OH, one P=O and two P–H bonds (monobasic). H₃PO₃ has one P–H; H₃PO₄ and H₄P₂O₇ have none.

questions.question: Which ore is usually concentrated by froth flotation?
questions.explanation: Froth flotation is used for sulphide ores; galena is PbS. Haematite and cassiterite are oxides (gravity/magnetic methods) and bauxite is leached.

questions.question: Which complex is an inner-orbital (d²sp³) complex and diamagnetic?
questions.explanation: Co³⁺ (d⁶) with NH₃ is low spin: all six electrons paired in t₂g, d²sp³ hybridised. [CoF₆]³⁻ and [Fe(H₂O)₆]²⁺ are high spin; [MnCl₄]²⁻ is sp³ with 5 unpaired electrons.

questions.question: The total number of stereoisomers of 2,3-dibromobutane is
questions.explanation: Two stereocentres with identical substitution: (2R,3R), (2S,3S) enantiomers and one meso form = 3.

questions.question: The number of structurally isomeric alcohols with the molecular formula C₅H₁₂O is
questions.explanation: Pentan-1-ol, pentan-2-ol, pentan-3-ol, 2-methylbutan-1-ol, 2-methylbutan-2-ol, 3-methylbutan-2-ol, 3-methylbutan-1-ol and 2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol = 8.

questions.question: Benzene reacts with 1-chloro-2-methylpropane, (CH₃)₂CHCH₂Cl, in the presence of anhydrous AlCl₃. The major product is
questions.explanation: The primary carbocation (or its AlCl₃ complex) rearranges by a 1,2-hydride shift to the tertiary (CH₃)₃C⁺, which alkylates benzene to give tert-butylbenzene.

questions.question: (R)-2-Bromobutane reacts with aqueous NaOH by an SN2 mechanism. The product is
questions.explanation: SN2 proceeds with backside attack and Walden inversion. OH replaces Br with the same priority ranking, so R becomes S.

questions.question: Which of the following cannot undergo aldol condensation?
questions.explanation: Aldol condensation needs an α-hydrogen. (CH₃)₃C–CHO has no α-H (it undergoes Cannizzaro reaction instead).

questions.question: Aniline is diazotised with NaNO₂/HCl at 0–5 °C and the product is treated with CuCN/KCN. The final product is
questions.explanation: Sandmeyer reaction: C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻ + CuCN → C₆H₅CN (benzonitrile) + N₂.

questions.question: Nylon-6,6 is obtained by condensation polymerisation of
questions.explanation: Nylon-6,6 is the polyamide of H₂N(CH₂)₆NH₂ and HOOC(CH₂)₄COOH; caprolactam gives nylon-6, glycol + terephthalic acid gives PET, phenol + HCHO gives bakelite.

questions.question: The number of onto functions from a set with 4 elements to a set with 3 elements is
questions.explanation: By inclusion–exclusion: 3⁴ − C(3,1)2⁴ + C(3,2)1⁴ = 81 − 48 + 3 = 36.

questions.question: The number of complex numbers z satisfying z̄ = z² is
questions.explanation: Taking moduli: |z| = |z|² ⇒ |z| = 0 or 1. z = 0 works. If |z| = 1, z̄ = 1/z so z³ = 1, giving three roots. Total 4.

questions.question: Both roots of x² − 2kx + k² − 1 = 0 lie in the interval (−2, 4) if and only if k belongs to
questions.explanation: The roots are k − 1 and k + 1. Need k − 1 > −2 and k + 1 < 4 ⇒ −1 < k < 3.

questions.question: a, b, c are in a non-constant geometric progression and a, 2b, 3c are in arithmetic progression. The common ratio of the GP is
questions.explanation: 4b = a + 3c ⇒ 4ar = a + 3ar² ⇒ 3r² − 4r + 1 = 0 ⇒ r = 1 or 1/3. Non-constant ⇒ r = 1/3.

questions.question: The number of non-negative integer solutions of x + y + z = 10 with each of x, y, z at most 5 is
questions.explanation: Total = C(12, 2) = 66. Solutions with x ≥ 6: x' + y + z = 4 ⇒ C(6, 2) = 15; times 3 variables = 45 (two variables ≥ 6 impossible). 66 − 45 = 21.

questions.question: The remainder when 7¹⁰³ is divided by 25 is
For A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]] (rows), A² = αA + βI. Then (α, β) equals
questions.explanation: Characteristic equation: λ² − (tr A)λ + det A = λ² − 5λ − 2 = 0. By Cayley–Hamilton, A² = 5A + 2I.

questions.question: Three fair dice are thrown. The probability that the sum of the numbers shown is 10 is
questions.explanation: Number of ordered triples (1–6) with sum 10 is 27 (coefficient of x¹⁰ in (x + … + x⁶)³). Probability = 27/216 = 1/8.

questions.question: A fair die is rolled 4 times. The probability that the largest number obtained is exactly 4 is
The number of solutions of sin 2x = cos x in the interval [0, 2π] is
questions.explanation: cos x(2 sin x − 1) = 0 ⇒ cos x = 0 (x = π/2, 3π/2) or sin x = 1/2 (x = π/6, 5π/6). Total 4.

questions.question: The length of the common chord of the circles x² + y² = 16 and (x − 6)² + y² = 16 is
questions.explanation: Subtracting gives the chord x = 3. Half-length = √(16 − 9) = √7, so the chord is 2√7.

questions.question: The normal to the parabola y² = 4x at the point (1, 2) meets the parabola again at
questions.explanation: (1, 2) is (at², 2at) with a = 1, t = 1. The normal at t meets the parabola again at t₂ = −t − 2/t = −3, i.e. (9, −6).

questions.question: The equation of the hyperbola (axes along the coordinate axes) with eccentricity 2 and distance between foci 16 is
The number of points in the open interval (0, 3) at which f(x) = [x²] is discontinuous ([·] = greatest integer function) is
questions.explanation: x² runs over (0, 9) and [x²] jumps whenever x² is an integer 1, 2, …, 8, i.e. at x = 1, √2, √3, 2, √5, √6, √7, √8: 8 points.

questions.question: The minimum value of f(x) = x² + 16/x for x > 0 is
The value of ∫ from 0 to π of x sin x/(1 + cos²x) dx is
questions.explanation: Using x → π − x: I = (π/2)∫₀^π sin x/(1 + cos²x) dx = (π/2)[−tan⁻¹(cos x)]₀^π = (π/2)(π/4 + π/4) = π²/4.

questions.question: The area of the region enclosed by y = |x| and y = 2 − x² is
questions.explanation: For x ≥ 0 the curves meet at x = 1. Area = 2∫₀¹ (2 − x² − x) dx = 2(2 − 1/3 − 1/2) = 7/3.

questions.question: The general solution of dy/dx = y/x + tan(y/x) is
questions.explanation: Put y = vx: x dv/dx = tan v ⇒ cot v dv = dx/x ⇒ ln sin v = ln x + c ⇒ sin(y/x) = Cx.

questions.question: If [a b c] = 4, the volume of the parallelepiped with coterminous edges a + b, b + c and c + a is
questions.explanation: [a+b  b+c  c+a] = 2[a b c] = 8.

questions.question: The image of the point (1, 2, 3) in the plane x + y + z = 0 is
